title: Does sizing positions by conviction (composite_score) instead of flat-equal splitting beat baseline on BOTH independent TRAIN and VAL $-compounding runs?

tables.name: Conviction-weighted sizing vs flat-equal baseline (5 tested)

notes: Extends full_strategy_simulation.py's simulate() with a new conviction_weight param -- blends equal-split sizing with composite_score-proportional sizing, same total dollars deployed per fill event either way. A single full-window (non-train/val) run showed every tested value beating flat-equal sizing (best: cw=1.0, $300->$337.61 vs baseline's $327.65) -- this calibration re-tests that properly, since day-level win_rate/std are expected to look nearly identical across conviction_weight values by construction (sizing doesn't change which trades happen or their % return), so the $-compounding outcome on independent TRAIN/VAL splits is the only metric that can actually validate or reject this.

conclusion.summary: 5/5 conviction_weight values beat flat-equal sizing's $-compounding outcome on BOTH independent TRAIN and VAL splits -- real candidate(s) for shipping, pick the specific value with human judgment (this project's convention is not to auto-select purely on this metric).
